newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam raps Buddists for harming national unity.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam raps Buddists for harming national unity.

text.p: Vietnam's Buddhist church has been told to stop dabbling in superstition, immorality and acts likely to harm religious and national unity, official media reports said on Monday.
The warning, from Politburo member Pham The Duyet, came at a time of heightened scrutiny of the communist country's sole legitimate church body, the Vietnam Buddhist Church (VBC).

"It (the VBC) should seek to overcome failings and negativeness such as superstition...committing immoral acts, violating commandments and the law, causing disorder and disunity or causing harm to religious and non-religious unity and national unity," the Lao Dong newspaper quoted Duyet as saying.

The Vietnam News Agency quoted him as telling the VBC central committee that it should strive for "closer Buddhist solidarity and national unity as a whole and against any attempt to undermine Vietnamese Buddhism and the country from abroad".
The government last week slammed an overseas Buddhist watchdog group, calling its report of dissent within the church over government interference "sheer fabrication".

The Paris-based International Buddhist Information Bureau's report had said that two senior VBC officials in Lam Dong province resigned because security forces arrested a superior monk and destroyed his pagoda.

"Their resignation followed a government clampdown against Buddhists in Lam Dong province in which security police arrested Thich Minh Dao...,superior monk of Long Tho Pagoda near Dalat, expelled 34 resident monks and nuns and subsequently razed the pagoda's 15 buildings to the ground," the group said.
However, the government said Thich Tu Man was still chairman of the Lam Dong VBC's Provincial Executive Committee and that his deputy, Thich Tam Thanh, had asked to retire due to poor health.
It also said that Long Tho Pagoda had been nothing more than a front for a man who pretended to be a monk, occupied public land, duped and deluded people and sexually abused women.

Many Buddhists who were forced to join the VBC after it was set up in 1981, including many now living abroad, still regard the outlawed Unified Buddhist Church of Vietnam (UBCV) as the country's sole legitimate church organisation.
The UBCV was the Buddhist church in former South Vietnam until the victory of Hanoi's communist forces over the south in 1975.
